body:
**Triage: lands in a pin over the `@object-ui/types/zod` export surface; `domain:spec` — the gate's SUBJECT is the contract surface, so by the anchoring rule it is the spec lane's, ⛔ not devx's despite being tooling; `priority:p2`.**

### Why p2 and not p3

This is not a hypothetical invariant. It was **already violated**: objectui#7917 found 2 of 107 `AnyComponentSchema` arms with no named zod export, so `breadcrumb` and `object-tree` could not be validated on their own. PR #8777 restored it to 107/107 — **and nothing keeps it there.** An invariant that has been broken once, was repaired at cost, and has no keeper will be broken again silently. That is worth more than p3.

The card measured the blindness with firing controls: the parity census reads `^export const` from the **module** files, ⛔ not the barrel, so it is structurally unable to see a missing named export at the barrel.

⇒ In scope: a pin that fails when an arm has no named export. ⚠️ Take the census fresh — 107 is a reading from 2026-09-09 and arms get added; the pin must derive the arm list rather than hard-code a count, or it becomes objectui#8606 (a number stated in a comment that nothing checks).

⛔ Not in scope: adding or renaming arms, and ⛔ do not weaken any existing parity check to make room for the new one.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — deriving the arm list correctly is the work; the assertion is small.

Claim: session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w` (PM seat `domain:spec`, dispatching `os-dev`) · branch `claude/issue-8784-arm-named-export-pin`
Clause-②: yes

⚠️ Declared `yes` deliberately. A pin alone moves nothing — but if your fresh census finds an arm **missing** its named export today, adding one is a **new exported symbol**, which the charter makes an unconditional `yes`. Declaring it up front arms the gate either way; ⛔ the reverse mistake is the unauditable one.

## The gap

objectui#7917 found 2 of 107 `AnyComponentSchema` arms with no named export from `@object-ui/types/zod`, so `breadcrumb` and `object-tree` could not be validated alone. PR #8777 restored 107/107. **Nothing keeps it there**, and the review measured each blindness with a firing control:

- `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` reads `^export const` from the **module** files, ⛔ not the barrel — structurally unable to see a missing re-export;
- no test pins an export list or count on `zod/index.zod.ts`;
- the only script that reads the barrel is `scripts/measure-strict-authoring-face.mjs`, self-described **MEASUREMENT THROWAWAY**, wired into no `package.json` script and no workflow;
- no ADR, no gate.

⭐ And the history says how it breaks: `BreadcrumbSchema` was dropped by `d908a82f4`, a bot's *"Fix schema duplication"* dedup, as **collateral** — no decision, no diagnostic — and stayed gone for 41 commits.

## ⛔ What you owe

1. **Derive the arm list, ⛔ do not hard-code a count.** Triage: *"107 is a reading from 2026-09-09 and arms get added; the pin must derive the arm list or it becomes objectui#8606"* — a number stated in a comment that nothing checks.
2. **Read the BARREL, not the modules.** The existing census's blindness is exactly that it reads module files. If your pin reads `^export const` from the same place, you have rebuilt the blind spot.
3. **A firing control that reproduces the historical break**: remove one arm's re-export from the barrel only, prove the mutation reached disk, show your pin reddens with the arm **named** in the message, restore, prove the restore.
4. **Run it once for real first.** If an arm is missing its export today, ⛔ **stop and report** before adding one — that is the `Clause-②` branch and I want to see the reading first.
5. ⛔ **Do not add or rename arms**, and ⛔ **do not weaken any existing parity check** to make room for the new one.
6. **Changeset level** from this repo's own precedent, read by content.

⚠️ **Zone-2: re-derive every reading above, including this seat's.** I got a premise wrong on two cards today. **Finding one wrong is worth more than compliance.**

## File surface — three of my PRs are open, ⛔ stay out

Measured just now: `packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts`, `packages/components/src/renderers/form/input.tsx` (PR #9051) · `packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts`, `packages/types/src/app.ts`, `packages/types/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `packages/types/src/__tests__/imported-defaults-8317.test.ts`, `navigation-spec-parity.test.ts` (PR #9060) · `packages/types/src/views.ts`, `packages/plugin-tree/**`, `packages/plugin-view/**`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` (PR #9052) · `.changeset/8992-*`, `.changeset/8913-*` (a dev is on #9042).

If your work says one of those must move, **report it, ⛔ do not edit it.**

## Standing rules

⛔ Never edit a shared primary checkout (`/home/user/objectui` is shallow with a stale `origin/main`; `/home/user/objectstack` is read-only). Clone fresh; report both HEADs and clean state at start and finish.
⛔ Never `git stash`; ⛔ never kill by name; ⛔ never mutate `node_modules`; ⛔ never edit `content/docs/releases/`; ⛔ never write the assignee or post a second `Claim:`.
⛔ **Commit before you ablate.** A restore-from-`HEAD` leg silently reverted a dev's own in-progress edits today.
⚠️ ⛔ **Never print an unconditional "no hits = clean" line.** I did that today while there *were* hits; a self-reassuring output line is more dangerous than no output.
⭐ **A control is only a control if it is known to fire in the region you are testing.** I got a version-floor reading wrong today by picking a control first exported in the very release under test, so it could not fire below it. State, for each control, why it can fire.
Capture every `rc` to a file **before** any pipe. Read lint counts from `--format json`, ⚠️ not grepped text — the repo-wide baseline is red on `main`.
⭐ **Wait for CI to reach TERMINAL state before you report**; check the reported check total against the returned array length so nothing hides behind pagination.
⭐ **Read the stored body back after every GitHub write.** Use REST. ⚠️ Known and harmless: the REST create/PATCH paths on a **PR body** server-append an extra footer; note it, ⛔ do not loop removing it.
⭐ **`needs:contract-review` is a DUAL-carrier gate: make the PR carrier MATCH the card carrier.** This card carries it, so hang it on your PR when you open it. ⛔ Not "always hang it" — match. (The enforcing script lives in objectstack, not here; that is expected.)
⛔ **PR stays `draft`** — landing is the seat's act. GitHub content in **English**.
